question.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $C(1,\sqrt{2},-1)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨0,11,\frac{1}{3}⟩+s⟨1,2,-3⟩$ and $r=⟨0,\sqrt{2},5⟩+t⟨-1,0,3⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨1,2,-3⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨-1,0,3⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $C(1,\sqrt{2},-1)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $c=⟨1,\sqrt{2},-1⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =c+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨1,\sqrt{2},-1⟩+s⟨1,2,-3⟩+t⟨-1,0,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
